human-environment-two-views.alt: Left: environmental determinism, an idea of the late 1800s and early 1900s: an arrow says the physical environment, climate and land, decides how people live and behave. Right: possibilism, the view that replaced it: the physical environment sets limits and offers options, and a two-way arrow says people choose, as culture and technology shape how they use it. A note says determinism was used to claim that people in hot climates could not govern themselves, an argument for colonial rule, and that geographers rejected it.

human-environment-terraces.alt: A drawn scene of a steep, forested hillside cut into seven narrow, flat steps of green crops, each held up by a low stone wall. A small channel carries water down the slope beside the steps. Two houses stand near a river at the foot of the hill.
